variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: HashiCorp Vault is an identity-aware control plane for secrets and cryptographic operations. A client proves an external identity, Vault issues a bounded token, policy authorizes exact paths and capabilities, and a secrets engine stores, generates, transforms, or revokes material.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Authenticate
pairs.detail: An auth method validates Kubernetes, cloud IAM, OIDC, LDAP, AppRole, certificate, or other evidence and maps it to Vault token policy.
pairs.explanation: An auth method validates Kubernetes, cloud IAM, OIDC, LDAP, AppRole, certificate, or other evidence and maps it to Vault token policy.

pairs.label: Authorize
pairs.detail: Path-based policy grants explicit capabilities such as read, create, update, list, or delete.
pairs.explanation: Path-based policy grants explicit capabilities such as read, create, update, list, or delete. Authentication alone grants no secret access.

pairs.label: Broker
pairs.detail: Secret engines version static data, create dynamic external identities, issue certificates, or perform cryptographic operations.
pairs.explanation: Secret engines version static data, create dynamic external identities, issue certificates, or perform cryptographic operations.

pairs.label: Account
pairs.detail: Audit devices record API requests and responses, usually HMAC-hashing sensitive string values while preserving enough identity for investigation.
pairs.explanation: Audit devices record API requests and responses, usually HMAC-hashing sensitive string values while preserving enough identity for investigation.

variants.hint:
Authenticate: An auth method validates Kubernetes, cloud IAM, OIDC, LDAP, AppRole, certificate, or other evidence and maps it to Vault token policy.

Authorize: Path-based policy grants explicit capabilities such as read, create, update, list, or delete.

Broker: Secret engines version static data, create dynamic external identities, issue certificates, or perform cryptographic operations.

Account: Audit devices record API requests and responses, usually HMAC-hashing sensitive string values while preserving enough identity for investigation.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.label: Authenticate the workload
pairs.detail: Validate short-lived platform evidence and map identity metadata to a tightly bounded token role.
pairs.explanation: Validate short-lived platform evidence and map identity metadata to a tightly bounded token role.

pairs.label: Authorize one role
pairs.detail: Permit only the required database credential path and token self-service operations; keep engine configuration under a separate operator policy.
pairs.explanation: Permit only the required database credential path and token self-service operations; keep engine configuration under a separate operator policy.

pairs.label: Create and lease
pairs.detail: Ask the database plugin to create a unique login, store lease metadata, audit the response, and return the credential with TTL and lease ID.
pairs.explanation: Ask the database plugin to create a unique login, store lease metadata, audit the response, and return the credential with TTL and lease ID.

pairs.label: Renew, replace, or revoke
pairs.detail: Renew before expiry when allowed, reacquire on rotation, and revoke the token tree when identity or workload ownership ends.
pairs.explanation: Renew before expiry when allowed, reacquire on rotation, and revoke the token tree when identity or workload ownership ends.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: HashiCorp Vault is an identity-aware control plane for secrets and cryptographic operations. A client proves an external identity, Vault issues a bounded token, policy authorizes exact paths and capabilities, and a secrets engine stores, generates, transforms, or revokes material.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: KV v2
pairs.detail: Stores application-managed values with version history and deletion controls.
pairs.explanation: Stores application-managed values with version history and deletion controls. Copying a value out of Vault creates a separate rotation and exposure boundary.

pairs.label: Dynamic engines
pairs.detail: Database, cloud, Kubernetes, PKI, and other engines can generate target-system credentials or identities with engine-specific TTL and revocation behavior.
pairs.explanation: Database, cloud, Kubernetes, PKI, and other engines can generate target-system credentials or identities with engine-specific TTL and revocation behavior.

pairs.label: Transit
pairs.detail: Encrypts, decrypts, signs, verifies, or derives data without returning the protected key to the caller.
pairs.explanation: Encrypts, decrypts, signs, verifies, or derives data without returning the protected key to the caller. Application ciphertext and key-version migration remain explicit.

variants.hint:

Dynamic engines: Database, cloud, Kubernetes, PKI, and other engines can generate target-system credentials or identities with engine-specific TTL and revocation behavior.

Transit: Encrypts, decrypts, signs, verifies, or derives data without returning the protected key to the caller.
